tracks.narration: What if a vector were not an arrow at all — but a polynomial?
A polynomial of degree at most two is a plus b x plus c x squared. Three numbers a, b, c spell out the whole curve. Those three numbers are its coordinates in the basis one, x, and x squared.
Now turn the dials. As a moves the curve up and down, b tilts it, and c bends it. Three numbers, one curve — they move together.
Add two polynomials by adding their coordinate triples one row at a time. The graph of p plus q is exactly the curve whose coordinates are the sum.
Polynomials of degree at most two form a three-dimensional vector space. The basis is one, x, x squared — the coordinates are the polynomial.
